text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 2.7% today as oil prices and refining profits surged. Crude is trading at $103 per barrel in the US and $123 globally, and refiners' earnings have spiked sharply as Ukrainian and Iranian attacks disrupted Russian and Middle Eastern refineries, tightening fuel supplies worldwide. Competitor stocks like Chevron and Exxon hit all-time highs on the same tailwinds, lifting the sector broadly.

The stock has climbed 5% over two weeks as geopolitical tension in key oil-producing regions—particularly the Strait of Hormuz, where tankers are now running higher risks but earning premium freight rates—keeps crude and fuel prices elevated. This environment is directly translating to fatter profit margins for integrated oil companies that both produce crude and refine it into gasoline and diesel.
